_comment: Session-scoped safety net for the orchestrator, passed via `claude --settings`.
Verified on Claude Code 2.1.197: deny rules are evaluated BEFORE the permission mode,
so these still hold under --dangerously-skip-permissions. Everything not listed here
runs without a prompt.
Absolute paths need the double-slash form: Edit(//home/... ), not Edit(/home/... ).
Use Edit(path) only — it covers every file-editing tool including Write. A Write(path)
rule is silently ineffective for file permission checks (2.1.220 warns about it).
Loosen freely — this is a backstop against irreversible accidents, not a policy.
The .claude and cc-orchestra denies exist so the hierarchy cannot rewrite its own
instructions mid-run. ~/.claude/orchestra is a symlink to the repo, so BOTH paths are
listed — permission checks resolve the real path, and denying only the symlink would
leave the repo writable. Edit the harness from an ordinary `claude` session instead.
The hook tells Tier 1 when orch-model-guard has moved the tier to another model, since a
running session's own model cannot be changed from outside. It is registered here AND in
~/.claude/settings.json on purpose: this file is only read at startup (so it covers every
new cc-orch session), settings.json is watched (so it reaches sessions already running).
The hook de-duplicates per prompt, so loading it twice still prints one notice.
PreToolUse worktree protection denies classified lead/dev Git collisions and is also installed in user settings.
SubagentStop validates lead gate-result claims with orch-summary-check --strict and is also installed in user settings.
SessionStart(compact) re-injects the registry, slot board and DIRECTIVES.md after compaction and is also installed in user settings.
